purpose: Records Advanced-tier controls that are explicitly N/A for a solo digital garden. Prevents over-building / enterprise theater. audit-rail-barrier-class.sh consults this file for signed friction-waivers. Peat's signature on each entry is the human gate.

scope_na_controls.reason: Solo garden — no hardware security module / TPM; no shared org identity infrastructure. Platform-default process isolation accepted.
Requires hardware attestation chip. Not available and not justified for a single-operator project.
microVM / Kata-container style execution isolation exceeds the risk profile of a personal website. OS-level process isolation is the appropriate ceiling.

scope_na_controls.control: JIT/JEA with auto-expiry (Just-In-Time / Just-Enough-Access credential issuance)
scope_na_controls.reason: Single operator with no external IdP. Session-scoped permissions in settings.json is the practical equivalent.

scope_na_controls.control: mTLS with certificate pinning (mutual TLS full lifecycle)
scope_na_controls.reason: No inter-service API calls requiring mutual TLS. Claude Code session transport handled by platform. N/A for local agentic tooling.

scope_na_controls.control: OS-level sandboxing (seccomp / AppArmor / network namespace / restricted mounts)
scope_na_controls.reason: Platform-default sandboxing accepted. Adding seccomp profiles to a local dev environment adds complexity without meaningful risk reduction for a solo operator.
Local append-only audit logs (signature files, hook-logs) are the appropriate logging tier. No external SIEM required for a solo garden.

scope_na_controls.control: Formal governance committee / automated compliance checks
scope_na_controls.reason: Single operator. Peat IS the governance committee. Policy is encoded in axioms-v1.json (Peat-signed).
No protected health information. Not applicable.
No financial data or regulated trading activity. Not applicable.
Personal website with no user data collection, no accounts, no analytics storing personal data. GDPR-by-design via no-collection posture.
Not a US federal system. Not applicable.

scope_na_controls.control: ML behavioral anomaly detection (contextual, Enterprise+ tier)
scope_na_controls.reason: Session volume too low for ML baselines to be meaningful. LLM judge (watchdog) in shadow mode is the appropriate residue.

_instructions: To activate a friction-waiver for a mode=block FRICTION-ONLY rail: add an entry to friction_waivers array with {rail_key, reason, signed_by: <Peat's explicit sign-off>, signed_date}. audit-rail-barrier-class.sh reads friction_waivers[]. Peat must set signed_by — agents may not self-sign.

rule_rationales.scope: FRICTION-strong (not HARD-barrier against determined adversary — OS sandbox is the correct ceiling)
rule_rationales.rationale: Peat 2026-06-03: a guardrail should block what causes DRIFT / is DANGEROUS — not block you from OBSERVING. The danger is exfiltration (sending data OUT) and fetch-execute (RCE), not fetching/observing (data IN to a file or stdout). Plain GET, -o/-O download, -sSL fetch, and sensor reads are observation / asset-vendoring. POST body (-d/--data/--data-binary/--data-raw/--data-urlencode/--json), form upload (-F/--form), file upload (-T/--upload-file), explicit mutating method (-X POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, including attached-verb forms -XPOST etc.), and pipe/chain to shell/interpreter (| sh, | bash, && bash) are blocked. -d@file (no-space), --data=@file (equals-form), and --data=value are all caught. -D/--dump-header (safe receive-to-file) is correctly NOT matched (case-sensitive flag check). Shell redirect to a real file (curl URL > /tmp/z) is caught by the redirect-deny rules (exit 0 removed from curl branch so redirect check runs). source/. <(curl URL) process-substitution RCE is blocked by a global structural deny before the curl branch. R5 (TASK-2026-06-03-CURL-WGET-ALGOL-R5): the command-position anchor is now a shared CMD_LEADIN recognizing not only ^ ; & | ( ) but also the brace-group token '{ ' (whitespace required after '{') and the compound-command keywords then/do/else/elif/until, so a curl/wget/source/interpreter first inside a brace group ({ curl -d … }) or right after a shell keyword (if …; then curl -d …) is no longer skipped. The INTERP and safe-tee right boundaries were widened from ([[:space:]]|$) to ([[:space:];&|)}]|$) so an interpreter or devnull-tee terminated by a shell metachar (| bash; }) is recognized. R6 (TASK-2026-06-03-CURL-WGET-ALGOL-R6): the fetch-execute chain operator class was widened from (&&|;) to (&&|;|&) so a lone background '&' separator (curl ... -o /tmp/x.sh & bash /tmp/x.sh, also & env/nohup bash) chains to an interpreter and blocks; and the pipe token was widened from \| to \|&? so bash's '|&' (pipe stdout+stderr) into an interpreter (curl ... |& bash) blocks. Both fire only when an interpreter follows, so a backgrounded or |&-piped fetch to a NON-interpreter (curl ... & ls, curl ... |& cat) stays allowed. R7 (TASK-2026-06-03-CURL-WGET-ALGOL-R6-INTERP-SMTP): the fetch-execute interpreter set was extended from the POSIX-ish base (sh|bash|zsh|dash|ksh|python|node|ruby|perl|php|lua|deno|bun|tclsh|Rscript|eval) to also cover stdin-executing interpreters/builtins/tools that were absent — INTERP_VER2 adds fish|csh|tcsh|xonsh|pwsh|julia|osascript|expect|gdb|awk|gawk|mawk, and INTERP_BUILTIN adds the source/. shell builtins (`.` matched only when followed by whitespace, so ./script and .bashrc are excluded) plus make and crontab (dangerous form make -f - / crontab - reads stdin). A fetch piped/chained into ANY of these now blocks (curl ... | fish, | osascript, | awk "{system($0)}", | source /dev/stdin, | make -f -). A Canopus self-pass also closed a pre-existing LEADING-PATH bypass affecting the base set too: an absolute/relative path to the interpreter (| /bin/bash, | /usr/bin/fish) slipped because the gate had no path prefix; every fetch-execute gate now consumes an optional LEADPATH=([^[:space:]]*/)? before the interpreter token (bare names consume zero and still match; | node_modules/.bin/foo and | ./postprocess.sh stay allowed). Finally, curl SMTP SEND egress (--mail-from/--mail-rcpt/--mail-auth, or an smtp(s):// target, case-insensitive) is now blocked — an emails-data-OUT channel that shared no token with the -d/-F/-T/--data*/--form*/--post-*/--method exfil set; IMAP/POP RETRIEVAL (imap(s)://, pop3(s)://, data IN) is intentionally NOT matched, preserving observe/download for mail fetch. Two independent adversarial passes found zero residual bypass and zero false positive.

Algol adversarial gauntlet 2026-06-03: source <(curl URL) and . <(curl URL) were previously silent-allow because the outer command is source/dot, not curl, so the curl-branch pipe-check never fired. Added a global structural deny in Phase 1 BEFORE the curl branch: blocks CMD_LEADIN[ 	]*(source|\.)[ 	]+<\( — any command boundary followed by source or . then a process-substitution. This is pure RCE (shell executing arbitrary remote content). Composes with existing $(...)/backtick metachar-eval warning but is a HARD-BLOCK, not a warn. R5: now uses the shared CMD_LEADIN (^ ; & | ( ) '{ ' then/do/else/elif/until) so { source <(curl URL); } and 'if …; then source <(curl URL); fi' are also blocked.
